title: Introduce inference health scorer and token-cost forecast panel
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a per-invocation inference health score metric and a Grafana forecast panel for token-cost prediction. New alert tuning uses forecasted burn to reduce alert churn. Backwards-compatible instrumentation; opt-out via feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Production teams want a single, explainable signal that summarizes invocation health (latency, cost, cache-warmth, model-fallbacks) and a short-term forecast of token burn to reduce noisy alerts during predictable bursts. This PR introduces a lightweight per-invocation 'inference_health_score' (0-100) plus a token-cost forecast panel that surfaces 1h/6h/24h EWMA forecasts and a confidence band.

What this changes (high level):
- Instrumentation: runtime emits 'inference_health_score', and additional tags: token_cohort, kernel_slot, hw_tier, prefix_warmth. Implemented in serving/telemetry/health_scorer.rs and runtime/tracing/span_enricher.cpp.
- Aggregation/worker: observability/pipelines/forecast_worker.go computes per-tenant EWMA forecasts for token-cost (tokens/sec and token-cost/sec) and writes forecast series to the metrics cache. Forecasts use an EWMA with adaptive alpha (short/long windows) and a confidence band from recent variance.
- Dashboard: grafana/dashboards/inference_health_and_forecast.json adds: health-summary heatmap, forecast sparkline (1h/6h/24h), cohorted bar (by token_cohort), and a causal-log-mosaic link column that deep-links into the trace inspector.
- Alerts: alerting/rules/forecast_slo_rules.yaml includes a forecast-aware alert rule that defers paging if projected 1h burn is within hysteresis threshold; it still fires if the health_score drops below 30 or if a critical fallback rate is observed.

Design notes:
- health_score composition: 40% latency SLO distance, 25% token-cost z-score, 20% prefix_warmth (higher is better), 10% kernel_queue_penalty, 5% recent-model-fallback-rate. The metric is normalized to 0-100 with guarded NaN handling. The algorithm is intentionally transparent (implemented as a deterministic rule in health_scorer.rs) to make RCA easier.
- Forecasting: we opted for EWMA-based forecasting to keep compute cheap in the ingest tier. The worker maintains short (1h), medium (6h), and long (24h) windows and exposes a 'forecast_confidence' derived from window variance.
- Alert tuning: new rule adds a 'forecast_quiet_window' if the projected burn explains the deviation; an 'explainability' label is attached listing the dominant contributor (e.g., "arrival_profile", "kv_cache_cold").

Backward compatibility & opt-out: default is enabled. For Dedicated/Private customers we provide an opt-out via config: observability.features.health_scorer=false. Metric names are stable and documented in docs/observability/metric_catalog.md.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests: health_scorer unit tests cover composition edge cases, NaN handling, and bucket assignment (tests/health_scorer_test.rs).
- Integration: forecast_worker was run in a staging replay (replaybench) for a 72h synthetic workload; dashboard panels validated against the replay and matched expected forecasts within 3% on average.
- Load: worker CPU and memorystore usage measured on staging 2x baseline with no observable impact on ingest pipeline; added a 50ms budget cap per-window evaluation to avoid tail amplification.

Files changed (high level):
- serving/telemetry/health_scorer.rs (+1 file, +210 + / -12) - new scoring logic and unit tests.
- observability/pipelines/forecast_worker.go (+1 file, +120 / -0) - forecast aggregation worker.
- grafana/dashboards/inference_health_and_forecast.json (+1 file, +45 / -1) - dashboard panels and links.
- alerting/rules/forecast_slo_rules.yaml (+1 file, +18 / -0) - alert rule with forecast deferral.
- docs/observability/metric_catalog.md (+1 file, +9 / -0) - documentation for new metrics.
- runtime/tracing/span_enricher.cpp (+1 file, +10 / -50) - minor span tag plumbing.
- ci/observability-tests.yml (+1 file, +0 / -26) - new CI job wiring for dashboard smoke tests.

PromQL examples used in panels (copied here for reviewer convenience):
- health score (per-tenant 90th): quantile_over_time(0.9, inference_health_score{tenant="$tenant"}[1m])
- token burn forecast sparkline: forecast_token_cost{tenant="$tenant", window="1h"}
- cohort breakdown: sum by(token_cohort) (rate(tokens_total[5m]))

Commits (summary):
- Add health scorer implementation and unit tests
- Add forecast worker and integration harness
- Add Grafana panels and alert rules
- Docs: metric catalog and rollout notes
- Fix linting and CI flakiness after initial run

Review conversation (abbreviated, inline):
- Ethan Morales (review): "Algorithm looks reasonable but please split the 40% latency bucket into two (initialization vs running) so we can debug cold-start vs in-flight latency impact."
- Maya Chen (author): "Done — split latency components in health_scorer and added test cases for cold-start contribution."
- Priya Singh (review): "Can we ensure forecasts can't be gamed by synthetic high-variance workloads? Add an upper cap to confidence band and a minimum-window sample requirement."
- Maya Chen: "Added min_samples=20 and capped confidence at 5x rolling stddev; added integration test in replaybench."
- Luca Bianchi (approve): "Nice visualization. One nit: include token_cohort in deep-link to trace inspector so downstream can filter."
- Maya Chen: "Added cohort param to deep-link and updated dashboard JSON."

CI summary: initial run (linux-unit-tests) failed lint (tools/clang-format) — fixed formatting in span_enricher.cpp and health_scorer.rs; re-ran end-to-end observability smoke which passed. New CI job ci/observability-dashboard-smoke was added and passed on staging GRP.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy forecast_worker to staging (done 2026-02-12) and run 72h replaybench.
2) Enable health_scorer (default on) in canary (5% tenant cohort) for 24h; monitor error budgets and dashboard.
3) Gradually ramp to 100% over 72h if no regressions.
4) For Dedicated/Private customers target release notes and an opt-out path.

Rollback: toggle observability.features.health_scorer=false in control-plane or roll worker to previous image. Metrics are additive; disabling removes scoring but does not affect raw latency or token metrics.

Notes for SRE/oncall: the alert rule includes an explanation label and a 'forecast_suppressed' counter; add to runbook: if many suppressed alerts coincide with a high forecast_confidence, treat as expected burst unless health_score < 30.

Thanks to the telemetry and frontend teams for pairing on the dashboard layout and to runtime for quick span-tag plumbing.
